Ming: quick update from today's RoPE sweep on Mixtral-8k. ran linear vs NTK vs YARN variants across head/kv dims, saw a reproducible divergence at seq=8192.
Raj: divergence how? perf or quality? :eyes:
Ming: both. latency and perplexity. NTK variant keeps stable latency but ppl jumps ~+0.9 for some prompts. linear keeps ppl but latency spikes with our default kernel selection.
Alice: do we have a minimal repro prompt? can we get exact ppl numbers and kernel traces?
Ming: yes. repro prompt is a concatenated doc (~6k tokens). short log snippet:
```
model: mixtral-8k
rope_variant: NTK
seq_len: 8192
kernel_selected: matmul_headslice_v1 -> matmul_headslice_v2 (fallback)
ppl_before: 2.31
ppl_after: 3.23
latency_95: 210ms -> 220ms
kv_cache_evictions: 0
batching_mode: continuous (size=4)
```
Sara: interesting that kv_evictions=0. but ppl jump w/out evictions suggests positional interpolation issue?
Ming: exactly. suspected RoPE scaling mismatch with head slice transforms. NTK introduces a different attenuation pattern, and our kernel's rotary application path doesn't match the quantized kernel math in some layers.
infra-bot: deploy-check: canary runtime configs applied to mixtral pool (canary id 20260321-3). :white_check_mark:
Raj: did you try forcing kernel matmul_generic instead of headslice to see quality diff?
Ming: yes — forcing `matmul_generic` yields stable ppl (2.34) but latency +30% across the board. So it's a tradeoff.
Alice: can we do selective kernel routing? e.g., use headslice for most layers but generic for layers with largest RoPE scale error?
Ming: prototyped a per-layer override list. quick patch:
```
# kernel routing override
overrides = {
  10: 'matmul_generic',
  11: 'matmul_generic'
}
```
results: ppl improved back to 2.36, latency delta reduced to +8% vs baseline.
Sara: promising. where's the batch heuristic fit in? you mentioned spikes with continuous batching.
Ming: when batcher groups heterogeneous seq_len profiles (mix of cached prefixes and fresh 6k prompts), kernel selection decision happens per-batch on predicted avg_seq. that pushes headslice for batch, but some tokens require generic -> jitter.
Raj: so batching heuristic mispredicted distribution leading to runtime kernel churn.
Alice: maybe use sequence-length bucketing before batching for ROPE-sensitive models. small extra scheduling cost but more stable kernel selection.
Ming: tried bucketing by prefix_length with 3 buckets: <2k, 2k-6k, >6k. latency 95 improved (reduced jitter), ppl stabilized for NTK case too but throughput down ~6%.
Sara: throughput drop acceptable if quality is restored. customers care about worst-case perplexity regressions.
Ming: agreed. next steps I propose:
- add per-model RoPE-variant metadata (linear|ntk|yarn) so router can pick initial kernel profile
- implement per-layer kernel overrides persisted in model config
- add seq-length bucketing to batcher for ROPE-sensitive models
- add a perf/eval job to run the small repro set on every kernel change
Raj: +1. can you file a small RFC and include perf numbers and the per-layer override script?
Ming: will do. I'll also attach the small repro set and a script to reproduce the ppl/regression locally.
Alice: please add an ETA for the RFC, and tag infra for canary rollout planning.
Ming: aiming EOD tomorrow for draft. tagging @Sara for eval thresholds.
Sara: cool. I can add alerting thresholds: ppl_regression > 0.5 or latency_p95 increase > 15% triggers rollback.
infra-bot: canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-22 03:00 UTC unless blocked.
Raj: thanks team. clean slate action items in the RFC will help ops and SRE.
Ming: leaving results and raw profiler traces on the mixtral-rope-sweep GCS bucket: gs://redwood-perf/mixtral/rope-sweep/2160001234/
Alice: great, i'll review after standup. :thumbsup:
